title: Range Module
prompt: A Range Module tracks ranges of numbers and tells you whether a given range is fully tracked. Design a `RangeModule` class supporting: `add_range(left, right)`, which tracks every real number in the half-open interval `[left, right)`, merging with already-tracked ranges as needed; `query_range(left, right)`, which returns `True` if every real number in `[left, right)` is currently tracked and `False` otherwise; and `remove_range(left, right)`, which stops tracking every real number in `[left, right)`, splitting existing tracked ranges as needed.

examples.input: add_range(10,20), remove_range(14,16), query_range(10,14) -> true, query_range(13,15) -> false, query_range(16,17) -> true
examples.explanation: After removing [14,16) from the tracked [10,20), the remaining tracked ranges are [10,14) and [16,20). [10,14) is fully tracked; [13,15) straddles the gap so it's not; [16,17) is inside [16,20) so it is tracked.
No range has ever been added, so nothing is tracked and any query_range call returns false.
Adding [1,5) and then [5,10), which touch exactly at 5, merges them into one continuous tracked range [1,10), so a query covering the full merged span returns true.

constraints: at most 10^4 calls total will be made to add_range, query_range, and remove_range
hints: Maintain the tracked ranges as a sorted list of disjoint, non-touching (left, right) intervals — similar in spirit to the Merge Intervals / Insert Interval problems, but supporting removal as well as insertion.

For add_range, find all existing intervals that overlap or touch the new range, merge them all together into one (extending min-left/max-right), remove the old ones, and insert the single merged interval back in sorted position.

For remove_range, find all existing intervals that overlap the range to remove; for each, keep only the portions before `left` and after `right` (if those portions are non-empty), replacing the original interval(s) with these leftover fragments. For query_range, use binary search to find a candidate interval and check if it fully contains [left, right).

solution.approach: Store tracked ranges as a sorted list of disjoint, non-adjacent (start, end) tuples, using the `bisect` module to locate insertion points in O(log n). For add_range, use bisect to find the span of existing intervals that overlap or touch [left, right), merge their bounds with the new range into one interval, and splice it in, replacing everything it absorbed. For remove_range, find all intervals overlapping [left, right), and replace each with 0, 1, or 2 leftover pieces (whatever remains outside [left, right)). For query_range, binary search for the interval whose start is <= left, and check whether its end is >= right; if so the whole query range is tracked.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n) per add_range/remove_range call, O(log n) per query_range, where n is the number of tracked ranges
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) to store the tracked ranges
